subject: Supply Chain & Logistics
title: Manufacturers and Assemblers
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Manufacturers and Assemblers.

hook.text: Foxconn doesn't design any product it makes. It builds iPhones, PlayStations, and Kindles for others.

buildup.text: Manufacturers transform raw materials into components. Assemblers combine components into products.

discovery.text: Contract manufacturers let brands outsource production while keeping design and marketing in-house.

twist.text: Outsourcing speeds scale-up but risks quality. You lose direct control of how your product is made.

climax.text: Tesla brought battery production in-house to control quality and cost. Not everyone can afford that.

punchline.text: Make it or outsource it. Both paths carry risk.

quiz.question: What does a contract manufacturer do?
options: Builds products designed by other companies
